title: Discovery and account-console interactions each emit one structured audit event on the fixed allow-list
asA: operator running the runtime-verify suite against the discovery client and the account-console verification
iWant: every named interaction on those two families to write one structured event carrying only the allow-list fields
soThat: the audit stream stays free of token material and a reviewer can decide at a glance whether an event field is inside the blueprint's contract

acceptanceCriteria.description: A completed discovery fetch for realm `alpha` emits exactly one `keycloak.discovery` audit event carrying `family=keycloak.discovery`, `outcome=verified`, `realmSlug=alpha`, and `at`; no other field appears.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a realm-config record for `alpha` whose issuer is reachable and whose discovery document responds 200
acceptanceCriteria.when: the discovery client fetches the realm's OIDC discovery document at boot
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one event whose own-property keys are exactly `{family, outcome, realmSlug, at}` with `family=keycloak.discovery` and `outcome=verified`; no token value, no client secret, no raw claim record, and no substring of any of the above appears in any field

acceptanceCriteria.description: A refused account-console verification against an unreachable `accountConsoleUrl` emits exactly one `keycloak.account_console` audit event carrying `outcome=refused` and `reasonClass=account_console_unreachable`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a realm-config record for `alpha` whose `accountConsoleUrl` returns 404 to an unauthenticated GET
acceptanceCriteria.when: the discovery client verifies the account console URL at boot
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one event whose own-property keys are exactly `{family, outcome, reasonClass, realmSlug, at}` with `family=keycloak.account_console`, `outcome=refused`, and `reasonClass=account_console_unreachable`; no token value, no client secret, no raw claim record, and no substring of any of the above appears in any field

acceptanceCriteria.description: A transient discovery failure followed by a successful retry emits exactly one refusal event and one verified event on the `keycloak.discovery` family, in order.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a realm-config record for `alpha` whose discovery endpoint returns 503 on the first attempt and 200 on the second
acceptanceCriteria.when: the discovery client retries per its documented retry posture and completes the fetch
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly two events in order: one `keycloak.discovery` event with `outcome=refused` and `reasonClass=upstream_unavailable`, then one `keycloak.discovery` event with `outcome=verified`; no additional event is written for the retry itself

acceptanceCriteria.description: A sink failure during the emission of a `keycloak.discovery` event does not mask the underlying discovery outcome; the mechanism records a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event and the discovery outcome is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a realm-config record for `alpha` whose discovery responds 200 and an audit sink whose write throws
acceptanceCriteria.when: the discovery client emits the completion event
acceptanceCriteria.then: the discovery outcome remains `verified` (boot proceeds); the mechanism records a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event carrying the realm slug and a reason-class string; no token value or raw claim record appears; the original refusal or verification result is not masked

acceptanceCriteria.description: A repeated identical discovery fetch of the same reachable realm (a scheduled `discoveryRefreshSeconds` refresh, or a second explicit fetch) is idempotent: each fetch call emits exactly one `keycloak.discovery` audit event with `outcome=verified`; two consecutive fetches produce two events (count is one per fetch call, never a deduplicated event).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a realm-config record for `alpha` whose issuer is reachable and whose discovery document responds 200 on every attempt, and a completed first fetch already on record
acceptanceCriteria.when: the discovery client performs a second discovery fetch against the same realm
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one additional event whose own-property keys are exactly `{family, outcome, realmSlug, at}` with `family=keycloak.discovery` and `outcome=verified`; the total count of `keycloak.discovery` verified events across the two fetches is exactly two; no additional event is written and no earlier event is mutated

acceptanceCriteria.description: A boot-time discovery fetch against a realm-config record whose `realmSlug` is a non-empty string (the credential that binds the fetch to a realm principal) emits a `keycloak.discovery` event that records that principal in the `realmSlug` field; a fetch attempted against a realm-config record whose `realmSlug` is missing or the empty string is refused before any network call with exactly one `keycloak.discovery` event carrying `outcome=refused` and `reasonClass=missing_realm_credential`, and no realm principal string leaks into any other field.
acceptanceCriteria.given: two realm-config records: record A for `alpha` whose `realmSlug` is `alpha` and whose discovery document responds 200; record B whose `realmSlug` is the empty string
acceptanceCriteria.when: the discovery client attempts a discovery fetch against each record in turn
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one `keycloak.discovery` event for record A with `outcome=verified` and `realmSlug=alpha` (the `realmSlug` field is the payload field that records the realm principal), and exactly one `keycloak.discovery` event for record B with `outcome=refused` and `reasonClass=missing_realm_credential`; no network call is issued for record B and no principal string appears in any other field

acceptanceCriteria.description: An account-console verification against a realm-config record whose `realmSlug` is present (a valid realm credential) but whose `accountConsoleUrl` origin differs from the discovered issuer origin (the record lacks the origin-scope the mechanism requires) is refused with exactly one `keycloak.account_console` event carrying `outcome=refused` and `reasonClass=account_console_malformed`; the event records the refusal reason and the realm principal, and the underlying account-console verification is not carried out.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a realm-config record for `alpha` with `realmSlug=alpha` whose discovered issuer origin is `https://issuer.example` and whose `accountConsoleUrl` origin is `https://other.example`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the discovery client verifies the account console URL at boot
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one event whose own-property keys are exactly `{family, outcome, reasonClass, realmSlug, at}` with `family=keycloak.account_console`, `outcome=refused`, `reasonClass=account_console_malformed`, and `realmSlug=alpha`; the `credentialSelfService` capability is not bound to the realm

description: Applying agent sets: no project-parameterised values on this story; every AC is `fixed`. AC-set sufficiency (7a inline note per blueprint-authoring.md §7a): the credential scenario class is bound by AC-6 (a realm-config record with a non-empty `realmSlug` is the credential the discovery fetch is bound to, and the `realmSlug` payload field records the realm principal; a missing credential is refused with `reasonClass=missing_realm_credential`). The permission scenario class is bound by AC-7 (a realm-config record whose `accountConsoleUrl` origin does not match the discovered issuer origin lacks the origin scope the mechanism requires and is refused with `reasonClass=account_console_malformed`).
